source.title: Accidental self-ignition of hydrogen released from pressurized cylinder
source.reported_apparatus: 50 L steel hydrogen cylinder at approximately 200 bar; controlled penetration used to emulate accidental breach
source.reported_instrumentation: internal pressure transducer at 0.2 s logging period; thermocouples at multiple distances/heights; high-speed and thermal imaging

files.name: Figure 7. Pressure drop during hydrogen release.xlsx
files.notes: The workbook contains trailing rows with missing time and negative/near-zero pressure values; no filtering or model fit is claimed here.

files.name: Figure 8. Hydrogen release and subsequent spark ignition.xlsx
files.notes: The archive provides six temperature columns but does not provide a machine-readable sensor-position mapping beyond the column labels.

files.name: Figure 9. Hydrogen release without ignition.xlsx
files.notes: The no-ignition trace is retained as a qualitative paired condition; the source reports sensor and environment limitations.

eligibility.reason_not_full_loop: The experiment is a controlled cylinder breach rather than a station-to-vehicle fueling event; breach geometry, discharge coefficient and complete calibration metadata are not supplied in the dataset record.

reported_findings.qualifier: Article-reported qualitative findings from three controlled cases; the observations do not estimate ignition probability or confirm a universal ignition mechanism.

findings: The open archive provides pressure and paired ignition/no-ignition temperature traces for a high-pressure accidental-release experiment.
The parent article reports ignition variability and delayed ignition several metres from the release point, making the data relevant to consequence and ignition scenario coverage.

The record is suitable for traceable safety-scenario grounding and future release/ignition model evaluation, but it must not be presented as a station full-loop validation set or as an ignition-probability estimate.
claim_boundary: This record establishes openly licensed experimental evidence and provenance for accidental high-pressure hydrogen release and ignition. It does not close the independent station-to-vehicle full-loop gate, prove an ignition probability, or validate the digital twin without a preregistered apparatus mapping and holdout protocol.
